Thanks for the issue! If you're reporting a bug, please be sure to include:
1. The version of ESLint you are using (run `eslint -v`)
2. What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)
3. The actual ESLint output complete with numbers
4. What you expected to happen instead

Requesting a new rule? Please see [Proposing a New Rule](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules) for instructions.

Looks like an issue with `estraverse` module.
I also verified that `espree` parses this code with no errors.

Quick question: Are you saying this used to work before with older versions of eslint?

Another example:

``` js
var f = ({method} = {}) => '';
```

_A lot_ of files in one of my project are causing these errors and it used to work.

It seems not connected to ESLint versions, thought. It worked when I used ESLint via `grunt-eslint@17.1.0` on September 9 so quite recently. `grunt-eslint@17.1.0` depends on `eslint@1.1.0` and now all ESLint versions from 1.1.0 to 1.5.1 fail on this code.

I cannot reproduce this in the online demo.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1937871/10126332/37c713b2-65cb-11e5-9473-c8c83d3107a3.png)

What is the version of `/Users/mgol/Documents/projects/bn/cbn/repo/polona-gui/node_modules/estraverse`?
ESLint requires `estraverse@4.1.0` or later.
If you are using `npm@3`, `npm@3` cannot install ESLint correctly (npm/npm#9663, npm/npm#9708).

Yeah, I've used npm@3, it works fine with npm@2.

I hope it gets fixed soon! Node 5 that will arrive in less than a month (next releases will come in 6 month intervals, this is the last release coming so shortly after the previous one) will have npm@3 included so breaking with npm@3 will mean not supporting Node 5.

I'm really hating npm 3 these days. Really sucks that they've broken peer dependencies so royally.

The only good solution here is for us to depend on estraverse directly and manually add in the JSX node references (basically, copy estraverse-fb into an ESLint source file).

This has been brought up previously in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/3890 as well.  

It sounds like there may be a fix coming upstream in NPM.  Is it worth adding the `blocked` label and waiting for that fix?
Let's just fix it on our side. I have little faith that an npm fix is coming soon.

never mind.
If there are other modules (such as `npm i eslint browserify`), it still reproduce this.

I had a similar error with `export default` and the patch estools/estraverse@c074451e7ab80dcedac4115a10a2ea31138d515c by @mysticatea (which was released yesterday) fixed it. Just make sure to install estraverse@4.1.1 as an explicit dependency, because npm@3 flattens the tree, otherwise a different package using a lower version of estraverse might override it.

issue.body:
I met this phenomenon use eslint@1.7.3 with browserify@12.0.1.
# Cause

I think a cause is that `estraverse-fb` use peerDependencies.
https://github.com/RReverser/estraverse-fb/blob/master/package.json#L19
# Steps to Reproduce
## npm install

```
npm i browserify eslint
```
## .eslintrc

```
{
  "env": {
    "es6": true
  },
  "ecmaFeatures": {
    "modules": true
  }
}
```
## log.js

```
export default function(...rest){
  console.log(...rest)
}
```
## Run

```
node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js log.js
```

issue.body:
Fixes #3951.

I'm not sure this PR's direction is right.

Currently there are cases that npm@3 does not install eslint correctly.
That cause is:
- browserify is depending on estraverse@1.9.3  
  (browserify -> module-deps -> detective -> escodegen -> estraverse)
- eslint is importing estraverse via estraverse-fb, then browserify's estraverse is imported wrongly.

```
<root>
├ browserify
├ eslint
│ └ estraverse@4.1.1
├ estraverse@1.9.3
├ estraverse-fb@1.3.1  <-- estraverse-fb is having estraverse in peerDependencies, 
                           so it should be installed into eslint directory. but...
...
```

So this PR imports estraverse and estraverse-fb severally, then it apply estraverse-fb to estraverse manually.

issue.body: This bit is taken from https://github.com/substack/node-detective/pull/58. Besides loading faster and taking up less space, it should _help_  with https://github.com/eslint/eslint/pull/4307 and https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/3951

body: Shouldn't be a problem a problem with browserify anymore - fixed by substack/node-detective/issues/59. Just `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` so your `browserify` pulls in a new version of `detective` that doesn't depend on `escodegen` (which had the problematic `estraverse`).
This is not related to browserify.

@nzakas It's the result of npm@3's new deduping algorithm. The issue manifests itself in projects that depend on both eslint and browserify – a common setup. I've demonstrated the issue here https://github.com/zertosh/eslint-npm-3-estraverse-dedupe-fail

When I say it's "fixed" in browserify, I mean it's worked around. browserify no longer uses an old estraverse, so for setups with eslint and browserify, this weird dependency issue won't manifest itself.
Yup. We are pretty clear on what problem is. Just making it clear to watchers that our issue is not related to browserify directly.
